content.thinking: I'll match each Pahawh Hmong glyph against every base letter and letter-plus-mark combination in Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong, the same approach used for Bamum.

input.command:
mkdir -p data_lake/downloads/fonts/noto-pahawh-hmong && curl -sSL -m 60 -o data_lake/downloads/fonts/noto-pahawh-hmong/NotoSansPahawhHmong-Regular.ttf "https://github.com/notofonts/notofonts.github.io/raw/main/fonts/NotoSansPahawhHmong/unhinted/ttf/NotoSansPahawhHmong-Regular.ttf" && file data_lake/downloads/fonts/noto-pahawh-hmong/NotoSansPahawhHmong-Regular.ttf | cut -c1-70 && cat > scratch/hmong_match.py <<'EOF'
import io, numpy as np, resvg_py
from PIL import Image
from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont
F = 'data_lake/downloads/fonts/noto-pahawh-hmong/NotoSansPahawhHmong-Regular.ttf'
cmap = TTFont(F).getBestCmap()
im = Image.open('data_lake/downloads/indigenous-of-asia/Indigenous of Asia.png').convert('RGBA')
ink = np.array(Image.alpha_composite(Image.new('RGBA', im.size, 'white'), im).convert('L')) < 128
cols = ink.any(0); xs = np.nonzero(cols)[0]
segs = []; s = xs[0]; p = xs[0]
for x in xs[1:]:
    if x - p > 3: segs.append((s, p + 1)); s = x
    p = x
segs.append((s, p + 1))
def render(t):
    svg = f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="400" height="300"><text x="100" y="220" font-size="150" font-family="Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong">{t}</text></svg>'
    r = Image.open(io.BytesIO(bytes(resvg_py.svg_to_bytes(svg_string=svg, width=400, font_files=[F], skip_system_fonts=True)))).convert('RGBA')
    return np.array(r)[..., 3] > 128
def crop(m):
    ys, xs = np.nonzero(m); return m[ys.min():ys.max() + 1, xs.min():xs.max() + 1]
bases = [c for c in range(0x16B00, 0x16B30) if c in cmap]
marks = [c for c in range(0x16B30, 0x16B37) if c in cmap]
cands = {chr(b): crop(render(chr(b))) for b in bases}
cands.update({chr(b) + chr(m): crop(render(chr(b) + chr(m))) for b in bases for m in marks})
# extra: other Pahawh signs (punctuation etc.)
for c in range(0x16B37, 0x16B90):
    if c in cmap:
        m = render(chr(c))
        if m.any(): cands[chr(c)] = crop(m)
out = []
for a, b in segs:
    g = crop(ink[:, a:b]); best = []
    for t, c in cands.items():
        T = np.array(Image.fromarray(c).resize((g.shape[1], g.shape[0])))
        iou = (T & g).sum() / (T | g).sum()
        ar = abs(np.log((c.shape[1] / c.shape[0]) / (g.shape[1] / g.shape[0])))
        best.append((iou - 0.3 * ar, t, round(float(iou), 2)))
    best.sort(reverse=True)
    out.append((a, b, best[:2]))
    print(a, b, [(' '.join('%X' % ord(ch) for ch in t), i) for _, t, i in best[:2]])
EOF
python -X utf8 scratch/hmong_match.py

"""Rebuild File:Itsukushima-island.png from MLIT 国土数値情報 N03 boundaries of 2000-10-01 (Hiroshima and Yamaguchi
municipalities, the era of the generalised File:Japan map.png the PNG was cut from): land white, sea #c0ffff, coast and
municipal borders #0000ff, Itsukushima (宮島町) green, in an equirectangular projection fitted to the PNG's land mask;
the 16 place labels as real <text> (transcribed, fitted to the PNG's lettering), and the leader lines, arrows and red
underlines as the PNG's own straight pixel runs. Run from the repo root."""
import io, json, sys, zipfile
import numpy as np, shapefile
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from scipy import optimize
from shapely.geometry import shape, box
from shapely.ops import unary_union, transform as stransform

sys.path.insert(0, 'tools')
from fit_text import fit  # noqa: E402

municipal borders #0000ff, Itsukushima (宮島町) green, in an equirectangular projection fitted to the PNG's land mask;
the 16 place labels as real <text> (transcribed, fitted to the PNG's lettering), and the leader lines, arrows and red

COS = np.cos(np.radians(34.25))
VIEW = box(131.9, 33.9, 132.7, 34.5)

H, W = im.shape[:2]

known = sea_px | land_px


def load(code):
    z = zipfile.ZipFile(f'data_lake/downloads/n03/2000/N03-001001_{code}_GML.zip')
    base = f'N03-001001_{code}-g_AdministrativeBoundary'
    r = shapefile.Reader(shp=io.BytesIO(z.read(base + '.shp')), shx=io.BytesIO(z.read(base + '.shx')),
                         dbf=io.BytesIO(z.read(base + '.dbf')), encoding='cp932')
    out = {}
    for sr in r.iterShapeRecords():
        g = shape(sr.shape.__geo_interface__)
        if g.intersects(VIEW):

          ('大黒神島', 20, 60, 95, 104, GREY, False), ('甲島', 22, 40, 107, 116, GREY, False),
          ('情島', 135, 145, 85, 104, GREY, True), ('長島', 67, 86, 110, 119, GREY, False),

input.content:
"""Rebuild File:Japan Chubu Region large.png from Natural Earth 10m admin-1 data (PD): Japan's 47 prefectures in a
Lambert conformal conic fitted to the PNG's land mask, the nine Chūbu prefectures in the PNG's dark green, the rest
in its light green, the southern Kuril Islands (claimed by Japan) in its pink, and Okinawa refitted into the PNG's
inset, whose rounded black frame is measured. Black coast, thin prefecture borders.
usage (repo root): python files/japan-chubu-region/build.py [fit]"""
import json, sys
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from pyproj import Transformer
from scipy import optimize
from shapely.geometry import shape, box
from shapely.ops import unary_union, transform as stransform

PNG = 'data_lake/downloads/japan-chubu-region/Japan Chubu Region large.png'
OUT = 'files/japan-chubu-region/Japan Chubu Region large.svg'
PAR = 'files/japan-chubu-region/projection.json'
NE = 'data_lake/downloads/natural-earth/ne_10m_admin_1_states_provinces.geojson'
LIGHT, DARK, PINK = '#94cf97', '#5f8f61', '#cf7d7d'
CHUBU = {'Niigata', 'Toyama', 'Ishikawa', 'Fukui', 'Yamanashi', 'Nagano', 'Gifu', 'Shizuoka', 'Aichi'}
INSET = (792, 1200)  # left and top of the inset frame (rounded corner, radius 200)

im = np.asarray(Image.open(PNG).convert('RGB')).astype(int)
H, W = im.shape[:2]
near = lambda c: np.abs(im - [int(c[i:i + 2], 16) for i in (1, 3, 5)]).sum(2) < 30
land_px = near(LIGHT) | near(DARK) | near(PINK)
yy, xx = np.mgrid[:H, :W]
in_inset = (xx > INSET[0] + 4) & (yy > INSET[1] + 4)

fc = json.load(open(NE, encoding='utf8'))
pref = {f['properties']['name']: shape(f['geometry']).buffer(0) for f in fc['features'] if f['properties']['adm0_a3'] == 'JPN'}
kuril_box = box(145.0, 43.2, 149.6, 45.7)
kurils = unary_union([shape(f['geometry']).intersection(kuril_box) for f in fc['features']
                      if f['properties']['adm0_a3'] == 'RUS' and shape(f['geometry']).intersects(kuril_box)])
main = {k: v for k, v in pref.items() if k != 'Okinawa'}
okinawa = pref['Okinawa']


def projector(p):
    lon0, lat1, lat2, s, tx, ty = p
    t = Transformer.from_crs('EPSG:4326', f'+proj=lcc +lon_0={lon0} +lat_1={float(np.clip(lat1, 5, 85))} '
                             f'+lat_2={float(np.clip(lat2, 5, 85))} +lat_0=36 +ellps=WGS84 +units=m', always_xy=True)

    def f(x, y, z=None):
        X, Y = t.transform(x, y)
        return np.asarray(X) * s / 1e4 + tx, -np.asarray(Y) * s / 1e4 + ty
    return f


def polys(g):
    return [q for q in (g.geoms if hasattr(g, 'geoms') else [g]) if q.geom_type == 'Polygon']


def raster(geoms, f):
    img = Image.new('1', (W, H), 0)
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    for g in geoms:
        for q in polys(stransform(f, g)):
            d.polygon(list(q.exterior.coords), fill=1)
            for r in q.interiors:

content.text:
This run is done and everything is pushed (20:39). The pause is lifted, and the queue is moving again.

- **New SVGs:**
  - **Indigenous of Asia:** a Pahawh Hmong sentence as real text in Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong; each letter was identified by matching it against every glyph in the font.
  - **Itsukushima-island:** rebuilt from the 2000 municipal boundary data (MLIT), with 17 transcribed Japanese labels as text. As with the other crops of the old generalised Japan map, the real coastline is busier than the original's.
  - **Japan Chubu Region large** and **Japan large:** rebuilt from Natural Earth prefectures, with the Okinawa inset fitted separately.
    - The build is now a reusable tool, `tools/japan_region_map.py`, for the rest of that map family.
    - In Japan large, Amami Ōshima is missing: the original moves it up the page, and at its real position it falls off the canvas.
- **Already on Commons as an SVG:** Historical expanse of Ainu. Its own page links a redrawn SVG of the same map, so I recorded that instead of redoing it.
- **Not rebuildable:**
  - **Idioma osetio:** the language areas are painted freehand.
  - **Ikushimatarushima shrine crest:** the kaji leaf is organic artwork, and the leaf on Commons is a different design.
- **Two items that earlier triage had already marked unrebuildable** are now off the queue.
- **Still blocked:** the arms waiting on your generator, which hasn't changed.

These new SVGs aren't in the zip I sent earlier. Say if you want a fresh upload package.

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy import ndimage
im=Image.open('data_lake/downloads/kaikatennou-oujintennou/Kaikatennou oujintennou.png').convert('RGBA')
a=np.array(Image.alpha_composite(Image.new('RGBA',im.size,'white'),im).convert('RGB')).astype(int)
ink=a.sum(2)<500
H,W=ink.shape
def runs(m,L):
    out=np.zeros_like(m)
    for y in range(m.shape[0]):
        r=np.concatenate([[0],m[y].astype(int),[0]]);d=np.diff(r)
        for s,e in zip(np.nonzero(d==1)[0],np.nonzero(d==-1)[0]):
            if e-s>=L: out[y,s:e]=True
    return out
lines=runs(ink,20)|runs(ink.T,20).T
txt=ink&~lines
lab,n=ndimage.label(ndimage.binary_dilation(txt,np.ones((9,3))))
red=(a[...,0]>200)&(a[...,1]<100)
for s in ndimage.find_objects(lab):
    ys,xs=np.nonzero(txt[s])
    if len(ys)<20: continue
    x0,x1,y0,y1=s[1].start+xs.min(),s[1].start+xs.max(),s[0].start+ys.min(),s[0].start+ys.max()
    print(x0,x1,y0,y1,'w',x1-x0+1,'red' if red[y0:y1+1,x0:x1+1].sum()>20 else '')
print('colours', np.unique(a[ink].reshape(-1,3),axis=0)[:5], 'size', W,H)
EOF

cat > files/kaikatennou-oujintennou/verticals.py <<'EOF'
"""Measure the anti-aliased vertical connector lines of Kaikatennou oujintennou.png (1 px lines drawn between pixel
columns, so they show as pairs of grey columns) and put them into spec.json as exact SVG lines ("extra"):
x is the darkness-weighted centre of each run, y its extent. Run before tools/rebuild_tree.py."""
import json
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

SPEC = 'files/kaikatennou-oujintennou/spec.json'
spec = json.load(open(SPEC, encoding='utf8'))
im = Image.open(spec['png']).convert('RGBA')
a = np.asarray(Image.alpha_composite(Image.new('RGBA', im.size, 'white'), im).convert('L')).astype(float)
dark = 255 - a
mask = np.zeros(a.shape, bool)
for x0, x1, y0, y1 in spec['mask']:
    mask[y0:y1 + 1, x0:x1 + 1] = True
ink = (dark > 40) & ~mask
H, W = a.shape
segs = []
for x in range(W - 1):
    col = ink[:, x] | ink[:, x + 1]
    r = np.concatenate([[0], col.astype(int), [0]]); d = np.diff(r)
    for s, e in zip(np.nonzero(d == 1)[0], np.nonzero(d == -1)[0]):
        if e - s < 12:
            continue
        w = dark[s:e, max(0, x - 1):x + 3]
        cx = (w * np.arange(max(0, x - 1), x + 3)[None, :]).sum() / max(w.sum(), 1) + 0.5
        segs.append((round(float(cx), 2), int(s), int(e)))
merged = []  # pairs of adjacent columns report the same line: keep one per (x, y-range)
for cx, s, e in sorted(segs):
    if merged and abs(merged[-1][0] - cx) < 1.0 and abs(merged[-1][1] - s) <= 2 and abs(merged[-1][2] - e) <= 2:
        continue
    merged.append((cx, s, e))
spec['extra'] = [f'<path d="M{cx},{s} V{e}" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1" fill="none"/>' for cx, s, e in merged]
json.dump(spec, open(SPEC, 'w', encoding='utf8'), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
print(len(merged), 'vertical lines:', merged)
EOF

content.text: Makasar script ("jangang-jangang", four letters). Using the same glyph-matching approach with Noto Serif Makasar.

input.command:
mkdir -p data_lake/downloads/fonts/noto-makasar && curl -sSL -m 60 -o data_lake/downloads/fonts/noto-makasar/NotoSerifMakasar-Regular.ttf "https://github.com/notofonts/notofonts.github.io/raw/main/fonts/NotoSerifMakasar/unhinted/ttf/NotoSerifMakasar-Regular.ttf" && file data_lake/downloads/fonts/noto-makasar/NotoSerifMakasar-Regular.ttf | cut -c1-60 && python -X utf8 - <<'EOF'
import io, numpy as np, resvg_py
from PIL import Image
from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont
F='data_lake/downloads/fonts/noto-makasar/NotoSerifMakasar-Regular.ttf'
cmap=TTFont(F).getBestCmap()
im=Image.open('data_lake/downloads/kata-jangangjangang/Kata jangangjangang.png').convert('RGBA')
ink=np.array(Image.alpha_composite(Image.new('RGBA',im.size,'white'),im).convert('L'))<128
lab_cols=ink.any(0); xs=np.nonzero(lab_cols)[0]
segs=[];s=xs[0];p=xs[0]
for x in xs[1:]:
    if x-p>5: segs.append((s,p+1)); s=x
    p=x
segs.append((s,p+1)); print(segs)
def render(t):
    svg=f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="500" height="400"><text x="100" y="300" font-size="200" font-family="Noto Serif Makasar">{t}</text></svg>'
    return np.array(Image.open(io.BytesIO(bytes(resvg_py.svg_to_bytes(svg_string=svg,width=500,font_files=[F],skip_system_fonts=True)))).convert('RGBA'))[...,3]>128
def crop(m):
    ys,xs=np.nonzero(m); return m[ys.min():ys.max()+1,xs.min():xs.max()+1]
cands={chr(c):crop(render(chr(c))) for c in range(0x11EE0,0x11EF9) if c in cmap and render(chr(c)).any()}
for a,b in segs:
    g=crop(ink[:,a:b]); best=[]
    for t,c in cands.items():
        T=np.array(Image.fromarray(c).resize((g.shape[1],g.shape[0])))
        best.append(((T&g).sum()/(T|g).sum()-0.3*abs(np.log((c.shape[1]/c.shape[0])/(g.shape[1]/g.shape[0]))),'%X'%ord(t),round(float((T&g).sum()/(T|g).sum()),2)))
    best.sort(reverse=True); print(a,b,best[:3])
EOF

Big part have to be with letters
*  8 Tsuka => A Tsuka

* C Sori => [1, 2, 3, 4 Nagasa/ 5 Shinogi, 6, 7 Ji, 8 Yokote]
* D Mono-Uchi => [1 Ha, 2 Hasaki, 3, 4]
* E Saya => 1 koigucchi, 2, 3, 4, [E-saya], 5 kojiri

python -X utf8 - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy import ndimage
a=np.array(Image.open('data_lake/downloads/kolkata-bus/Kolkata bus.png').convert('RGB')).astype(int)
u,n=np.unique(a.reshape(-1,3),axis=0,return_counts=True);o=np.argsort(-n)
cols=[tuple(u[i]) for i in o[:8]]; print([('#%02x%02x%02x'%c,n[i]) for c,i in zip(cols,o[:8])])
for c in cols[:7]:
    m=(np.abs(a-c).sum(2)<20); lab,k=ndimage.label(m)
    print('#%02x%02x%02x'%c)
    for s in ndimage.find_objects(lab):
        h=s[0].stop-s[0].start; w=s[1].stop-s[1].start
        if h*w>30: print('   x %d-%d y %d-%d'%(s[1].start,s[1].stop-1,s[0].start,s[0].stop-1))
EOF

import numpy as np, json
from PIL import Image
from scipy import optimize
a=np.array(Image.open('data_lake/downloads/kounoke-kamon/Kounoke kamon.png').convert('L'))<128
r0=np.nonzero(a[0])[0]; print('top row ink x',r0.min(),r0.max())
c0=np.nonzero(a[:,18])[0]; print('left col ink y',c0.min(),c0.max())
r=np.nonzero(a[58])[0]; print('row58 runs', r.min(), r.max())
ri=np.nonzero(~a[60,76:547])[0]+76; print('inner row60 white', ri.min(), ri.max())
ri=np.nonzero(~a[293,:])[0]; 
# band edges per column
xs=np.arange(156,469); edges={k:[] for k in range(6)}
for x in xs:
    c=np.nonzero(a[140:460,x])[0]+140
    runs=[(int(s),int(e)) for s,e in zip(c[np.r_[True,np.diff(c)>1]], c[np.r_[np.diff(c)>1,True]])]
    runs=[r for r in runs if r[1]-r[0]>40][:3]
    if len(runs)==3:
        for k,(s,e) in enumerate(runs): edges[2*k].append((x,s)); edges[2*k+1].append((x,e+1))
fits=[]
for k in range(6):
    p=np.array(edges[k]); X,Y=p[:,0],p[:,1]
    f=lambda q,X: q[0]+q[1]*np.sin(2*np.pi*(X-q[2])/q[3])
    best=None
    for P0 in (150,200,250,300):
        for ph in range(0,300,25):
            r=optimize.least_squares(lambda q: f(q,X)-Y,[Y.mean(),12,ph,P0])
            if best is None or r.cost<best.cost: best=r
    q=best.x; fits.append([float(v) for v in q]); print(k,[round(v,2) for v in q],'rms',round(float(np.sqrt(np.mean((f(q,X)-Y)**2))),2))
json.dump(fits,open('scratch/kouno_fits.json','w'))
EOF

import numpy as np, json
from PIL import Image
from scipy import ndimage
from shapely.geometry import MultiPoint
a=np.array(Image.open('data_lake/downloads/kounoke-kamon/Kounoke kamon.png').convert('L'))<128

def octagon(mask):
    ys,xs=np.nonzero(mask)

    for tol in np.arange(1,40,0.5):

EOF

import json

"""Rebuild File:Kōfukuji plan.png by construction: the plan is 1 px black lines drawn anti-aliased between pixel rows
and columns (so each shows as a pair of grey rows or columns). Every horizontal and vertical line is measured at its
darkness-weighted sub-pixel position and written as an exact segment; the two octagons (whose 45° edges are not
horizontal or vertical) are fitted as polygons to their outlines; the black triangle is its filled hull.
Run from the repo root."""
import glob
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy import ndimage
from shapely.geometry import MultiPoint

PNG = glob.glob('data_lake/downloads/kofukuji-plan/*.png')[0]
OUT = 'files/kofukuji-plan/Kōfukuji plan.svg'
a = np.asarray(Image.open(PNG).convert('L')).astype(float)
H, W = a.shape
dark = 255 - a
ink = dark > 30
black = a < 40


def lines(ink, dark, min_len=6):
    """horizontal lines: (y, x0, x1) with sub-pixel y from the darkness of the rows around each run"""
    segs = []
    for y in range(ink.shape[0]):
        r = np.concatenate([[0], ink[y].astype(int), [0]]); d = np.diff(r)
        for s, e in zip(np.nonzero(d == 1)[0], np.nonzero(d == -1)[0]):
            if e - s < min_len:
                continue
            w = dark[max(0, y - 1):y + 2, s:e].sum(1)
            cy = (w * np.arange(max(0, y - 1), y + 2)[:len(w)]).sum() / max(w.sum(), 1) + 0.5
            segs.append((round(float(cy), 2), int(s), int(e)))
    out = []
    for cy, s, e in sorted(segs):  # a line shows on two rows: keep one
        if out and abs(out[-1][0] - cy) < 1.0 and abs(out[-1][1] - s) <= 2 and abs(out[-1][2] - e) <= 2:
            continue
        out.append((cy, s, e))
    return out


# octagons: components whose outline has diagonal edges; find them by their bounding boxes in the PNG
lab, n = ndimage.label(ink)
octs, oct_mask = [], np.zeros_like(ink)
for i, sl in enumerate(ndimage.find_objects(lab), 1):
    comp = lab[sl] == i
    h, w = comp.shape
    if 25 <= h <= 70 and 25 <= w <= 70 and abs(h - w) <= 4 and comp[0, 0] == 0 and comp[0, w // 2] == 1:
        ys, xs = np.nonzero(comp)
        hull = MultiPoint(np.c_[xs + sl[1].start + 0.5, ys + sl[0].start + 0.5]).convex_hull
        for tol in np.arange(0.5, 6, 0.25):
            s = hull.simplify(tol)
            if len(s.exterior.coords) - 1 <= 8:
                break
        octs.append(s)
        oct_mask[sl] |= comp
tri = black & ~oct_mask
ty, tx = np.nonzero(tri)
tri_poly = MultiPoint(np.c_[tx + 0.5, ty + 0.5]).convex_hull.simplify(0.75) if len(tx) else None
lin_ink = ink & ~oct_mask & ~ndimage.binary_dilation(tri, iterations=2)
hs = lines(lin_ink, dark * lin_ink)
vs = lines(lin_ink.T, (dark * lin_ink).T)
d = ''.join(f'M{s},{y}H{e}' for y, s, e in hs) + ''.join(f'M{x},{s}V{e}' for x, s, e in vs)
d += ''.join('M' + ' '.join(f'{x:.2f},{y:.2f}' for x, y in list(o.exterior.coords)[:-1]) + 'Z' for o in octs)
svg = (f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{W}" height="{H}" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}">\n'
       f'<rect width="{W}" height="{H}" fill="#ffffff"/>\n'
       f'<path d="{d}" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1"/>\n'
       + (f'<path d="M' + ' '.join(f'{x:.1f},{y:.1f}' for x, y in list(tri_poly.exterior.coords)[:-1]) + 'Z"/>\n'
          if tri_poly is not None else '') + '</svg>\n')
open(OUT, 'w', encoding='utf8').write(svg)
print(len(hs), 'horizontal,', len(vs), 'vertical,', len(octs), 'octagons, triangle', tri_poly is not None)

darkness-weighted sub-pixel position and written as an exact segment; the two octagons (whose 45° edges are not
horizontal or vertical) are fitted as polygons to their outlines; the black triangle is its filled hull.

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy import ndimage
from shapely.geometry import MultiPoint

PNG = glob.glob('data_lake/downloads/kofukuji-plan/*.png')[0]
OUT = 'files/kofukuji-plan/Kōfukuji plan.svg'

H, W = a.shape

ink = dark > 30
black = a < 40

            segs.append((round(float(cy), 2), int(s), int(e)))
    out = []
    for cy, s, e in sorted(segs):  # a line shows on two rows: keep one
        if out and abs(out[-1][0] - cy) < 1.0 and abs(out[-1][1] - s) <= 2 and abs(out[-1][2] - e) <= 2:

This run is done and pushed (21:06). Eleven items left the queue: nine new SVGs and two marked not rebuildable.

**New SVGs, staged in `upload/`:**
- **Kaikatennou oujintennou:** a family tree with 13 names as real text. Its vertical connector lines sit between pixel columns, so I measured their exact positions rather than reading them as solid pixels.
- **Kata jangangjangang:** a Makasar-script word in Noto Serif Makasar. The original's letters are much wider, so the text is stretched 1.53× and still looks noticeably different.
- **KAWI LETTER OM:** a near-exact match (IoU 0.97), since the original was made from Noto Sans Kawi. It's the letter O plus a candrabindu mark, because Unicode has no separate Om letter. Its licence is the font's OFL, which can't be relicensed CC BY-SA, so I changed the upload packager to keep OFL for files like this.
- **Kharosthi font rendering sample:** the exact Unicode text from the file description. Noto stacks the characters differently from the font the PNG used.
- **Koshur in Sharada:** IoU 0.85, made from Noto Sans Sharada, the same font as the original.
- **Kolkata bus:** built from measured rectangles and the roof shape; 0.6% of pixels differ.
- **Kōno clan crest:** the octagon ring is fitted, and all six band edges follow a single fitted sine wave; IoU 0.98.
- **Kōfukuji plan:** every line placed at its measured sub-pixel position, plus two fitted octagons; essentially exact.
- **LFW2008 2403:** a Tangut character in Noto Serif Tangut. Noto draws it differently from the dictionary glyph in the original (IoU 0.32).

**Not rebuildable:**
- **Katana diagram:** a shaded painted illustration. The katana SVG on Commons is of a different diagram.
- **Koshiate:** a 1735 woodblock print.

The arms are still blocked, because your generator hasn't changed. These new SVGs aren't in the last zip; I can build a fresh upload package whenever you want one.

input.content:
"""Rebuild File:Map-okinawa-pref.png from MLIT 国土数値情報 N03 (2024) boundaries of Okinawa Prefecture: the islands in an
equirectangular projection (x scaled by cos 25.5°) fitted to the PNG's land mask, flat green (the PNG's islands carry
relief shading from a raster render, which is not reproduced), a dark green coast on the PNG's #ceffff sea, the star at
Naha, and every label as real <text> (transcribed; English in black or blue italic, Japanese below) fitted to the PNG's
lettering. Run from the repo root."""
import json, sys
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from scipy import optimize
from shapely.geometry import shape, box
from shapely.ops import unary_union, transform as stransform

sys.path.insert(0, 'tools')
from n03_prefecture_svg import load  # noqa: E402
from fit_text import fit  # noqa: E402

PNG = 'data_lake/downloads/map-okinawa-pref/Map-okinawa-pref.png'
OUT = 'files/map-okinawa-pref/Map-okinawa-pref.svg'
PAR = 'files/map-okinawa-pref/projection.json'
SEA, LAND, COAST, BLUE = '#ceffff', '#8ddc8d', '#4d7a4d', '#0000ff'
COS = np.cos(np.radians(25.5))

im = np.asarray(Image.open(PNG).convert('RGB')).astype(int)
H, W = im.shape[:2]
land_px = (im[..., 1] > im[..., 2] + 15) & (im[..., 1] > im[..., 0] + 10)
text_px = im.sum(2) < 300

geo = unary_union([shape(f['geometry']) for f in load(47)['features']]).intersection(box(122, 24, 132, 27.5))
isl = [g for g in (geo.geoms if hasattr(geo, 'geoms') else [geo]) if g.area > 2e-7]


def proj(p):
    s, tx, ty = p
    return lambda x, y, z=None: (np.asarray(x) * COS * s + tx, -np.asarray(y) * s + ty)


def raster(f):
    img = Image.new('1', (W, H), 0)
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    for g in isl:
        q = stransform(f, g)
        d.polygon(list(q.exterior.coords), fill=1)
        for r in q.interiors:
            d.polygon(list(r.coords), fill=0)
    return np.asarray(img)


def loss(p):
    m = raster(proj(p)) & ~text_px
    t = land_px & ~text_px
    return 1 - (m & t).sum() / (m | t).sum()


# (texts top to bottom, box x0, x1, y0, y1, colour, italic, size hint); a box holding two lines is split at its gap
LABELS = [(['Okinawa Prefecture'], 59, 327, 25, 45, '#000000', False), (['沖縄県'], 60, 137, 55, 80, '#000000', False),
          (['Okinawa Islands'], 568, 734, 32, 48, BLUE, True), (['沖縄諸島'], 612, 691, 55, 73, BLUE, False),
          (['Kume', '久米島'], 556, 603, 108, 143, '#000000', False), (['Naha', '那覇'], 711, 743, 116, 142, '#000000', False),
          (['Okinawa'], 802, 869, 130, 141, '#000000', False), (['Island'], 812, 859, 150, 161, '#000000', False),
          (['沖縄本島'], 809, 867, 169, 181, '#000000', False), (['Kerama Is.', '慶良間諸島'], 635, 708, 161, 189, BLUE, True),
          (['Senkaku'], 171, 237, 201, 213, '#000000', False), (['尖閣諸島'], 171, 237, 222, 236, '#000000', False),
          (['Miyako Islands'], 313, 464, 274, 289, BLUE, True), (['宮古諸島'], 349, 430, 296, 315, BLUE, False),
          (['Yaeyama Islands', '八重山諸島'], 71, 241, 324, 365, BLUE, True),
          (['Miyako', '宮古島'], 388, 441, 372, 404, '#000000', False),
          (['Yonaguni'], 31, 102, 415, 430, '#000000', False), (['与那国島'], 33, 99, 436, 449, '#000000', False),
          (['Ishigaki', '石垣島'], 237, 298, 422, 454, '#000000', False),
          (['Iriomote'], 121, 191, 430, 441, '#000000', False), (['西表島'], 134, 178, 449, 461, '#000000', False)]


def lines_of(texts, x0, x1, y0, y1, col):
    """split a two-line box at its widest empty row band and measure each line's ink box"""
    tm = (np.abs(im[y0:y1 + 1, x0:x1 + 1] - [int(col[i:i + 2], 16) for i in (1, 3, 5)]).sum(2) < 200) & \
         (im[y0:y1 + 1, x0:x1 + 1].sum(2) < 600)
    rows = np.nonzero(tm.any(1))[0]
    if len(texts) == 1:
        return [(texts[0], x0, x1, y0 + rows.min(), y0 + rows.max())]
    gaps = np.diff(rows)
    k = int(np.argmax(gaps))
    out = []
    for t, (r0, r1) in zip(texts, [(rows[0], rows[k]), (rows[k + 1], rows[-1])]):
        cols = np.nonzero(tm[r0:r1 + 1].any(0))[0]
        out.append((t, x0 + cols.min(), x0 + cols.max(), y0 + r0, y0 + r1))
    return out


if __name__ == '__main__':
    if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == 'fit':
        x0, y0, x1, y1 = geo.bounds
        ys, xs = np.nonzero(land_px)
        s = (xs.max() - xs.min()) / ((x1 - x0) * COS)
        p0 = [s, xs.min() - x0 * COS * s, ys.min() + y1 * s]
        r = optimize.minimize(loss, p0, method='Nelder-Mead', options={'maxiter': 800, 'xatol': 1e-3, 'fatol': 1e-7})
        fits = []
        for texts, a, b, c, d, col, it in LABELS:
            for t, la, lb, lc, ld in lines_of(texts, a, b, c, d, col):
                fam = 'Arial' if not any(ord(ch) > 0x3000 for ch in t) else 'MS Gothic'
                fam_full = fam + (';font-style:italic' if it and fam == 'Arial' else '')
                q = fit(t, (la, lb, lc, ld), fam_full, 'normal', canvas=(W, H))
                fits.append(dict(text=t, colour=col, italic=it and fam == 'Arial', cjk=fam != 'Arial', **q))
        json.dump({'p': list(r.x), 'labels': fits}, open(PAR, 'w', encoding='utf8'), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
    P = json.load(open(PAR, encoding='utf8'))
    f = proj(P['p'])
    print('land IoU %.4f' % (1 - loss(P['p'])))
    d = ''.join('M' + ' '.join(f'{x:.1f},{y:.1f}' for x, y in r.coords) + 'Z'
                for g in isl for q in [stransform(f, g.simplify(0.0003))] for r in [q.exterior, *q.interiors])
    texts = []
    for q in P['labels']:
        fam = "'MS Gothic', 'IPAGothic', 'Noto Sans CJK JP', sans-serif" if q['cjk'] else "Arial, 'Liberation Sans', sans-serif"
        st = ' font-style="italic"' if q['italic'] else ''
        ls = f' letter-spacing="{q["ls"]}"' if abs(q['ls']) > 0.05 else ''
        texts.append(f'<text x="{q["x"]}" y="{q["y"]}" font-family="{fam}"{st} font-size="{q["size"]}"{ls} '
                     f'fill="{q["colour"]}">{q["text"]}</text>')
    nx, ny = f(127.68, 26.21)  # Naha
    star = ' '.join(f'{float(nx) + r * np.sin(np.pi * k / 5):.1f},{float(ny) - r * np.cos(np.pi * k / 5):.1f}'
                    for k, r in zip(range(10), [5.5, 2.2] * 5))
    o = [f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{W}" height="{H}" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}">',
         f'<rect width="{W}" height="{H}" fill="{SEA}"/>',
         f'<path d="{d}" fill="{LAND}" stroke="{COAST}" stroke-width="0.8" stroke-linejoin="round"/>',
         f'<polygon points="{star}" fill="#000000"/>', *texts, '</svg>']
    open(OUT, 'w', encoding='utf8').write('\n'.join(o) + '\n')
    print('wrote', OUT, len(isl), 'islands,', len(texts), 'labels')

input.content:
"""Rebuild File:Matsuura-gun.png from MLIT 国土数値情報 N03 boundaries of 2000-10-01 (Fukuoka, Saga, Nagasaki, Kumamoto
municipalities; the era of the generalised File:Japan map.png the PNG was cut from): Saga and Nagasaki land white,
other prefectures grey, the municipalities the PNG shows yellow (Meiji-era Matsuura District) in yellow, coast blue,
municipal borders black, prefecture borders red, in an equirectangular projection fitted to the PNG's land mask. The
sea boundary lines are the PNG's own pixel runs; the legend (現在 / 明治期 / 郡役所) is constructed, its labels real
<text>. Run from the repo root."""
import io, json, sys, zipfile
import numpy as np, shapefile
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from scipy import optimize, ndimage
from shapely.geometry import shape, box
from shapely.ops import unary_union, transform as stransform

sys.path.insert(0, 'tools')
from fit_text import fit  # noqa: E402

PNG = 'data_lake/downloads/matsuura-gun/Matsuura-gun.png'
OUT = 'files/matsuura-gun/Matsuura-gun.svg'
PAR = 'files/matsuura-gun/projection.json'
SEA, LAND, GREY, YELLOW, COAST, RED = '#64fefe', '#ffffff', '#dadada', '#ffff00', '#0000fe', '#fa0000'
COS = np.cos(np.radians(33.2))
VIEW = box(128.3, 32.3, 130.5, 34.8)
LEGEND = (229, 281, 400, 433)

im = np.asarray(Image.open(PNG).convert('RGB')).astype(int)
H, W = im.shape[:2]
near = lambda c, t=12: np.abs(im - [int(c[i:i + 2], 16) for i in (1, 3, 5)]).sum(2) < t
sea_px = near(SEA, 20)
yellow_px = near(YELLOW)
land_px = near(LAND) | near(GREY) | yellow_px | near('#dedede')
lx0, lx1, ly0, ly1 = LEGEND
in_legend = np.zeros((H, W), bool)
in_legend[ly0 - 1:ly1 + 2, lx0 - 1:lx1 + 2] = True
known = (sea_px | land_px) & ~in_legend


def load(code):
    z = zipfile.ZipFile(f'data_lake/downloads/n03/2000/N03-001001_{code}_GML.zip')
    base = f'N03-001001_{code}-g_AdministrativeBoundary'
    r = shapefile.Reader(shp=io.BytesIO(z.read(base + '.shp')), shx=io.BytesIO(z.read(base + '.shx')),
                         dbf=io.BytesIO(z.read(base + '.dbf')), encoding='cp932')
    out = {}
    for sr in r.iterShapeRecords():
        g = shape(sr.shape.__geo_interface__)
        if g.intersects(VIEW):
            out.setdefault((code, sr.record[2], sr.record[3]), []).append(g.intersection(VIEW))
    return {k: unary_union(v).buffer(0) for k, v in out.items()}


munis = {}
for c in ('40', '41', '42', '43'):
    munis.update(load(c))
land = unary_union(list(munis.values()))
prefs = {c: unary_union([g for k, g in munis.items() if k[0] == c]) for c in ('40', '41', '42', '43')}


def proj(p):
    s, tx, ty = p
    return lambda x, y, z=None: (np.asarray(x) * COS * s + tx, -np.asarray(y) * s + ty)


def polys(g):
    return [q for q in (g.geoms if hasattr(g, 'geoms') else [g]) if q.geom_type == 'Polygon' and not q.is_empty]


def raster(g, f):
    img = Image.new('1', (W, H), 0)
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    for q in polys(stransform(f, g)):
        d.polygon(list(q.exterior.coords), fill=1)
        for rr in q.interiors:
            d.polygon(list(rr.coords), fill=0)
    return np.asarray(img)


def loss(p):
    m = raster(land, proj(p))
    return 1 - ((m & land_px) & known).sum() / ((m | land_px) & known).sum()


def d_of(g, f, close=True):
    return ''.join('M' + ' '.join(f'{x:.1f},{y:.1f}' for x, y in rr.coords) + ('Z' if close else '')
                   for q in polys(stransform(f, g)) for rr in [q.exterior, *q.interiors])


def line_d(g, f):
    out = []
    for q in (g.geoms if hasattr(g, 'geoms') else [g]):
        if q.geom_type == 'LineString':
            out.append('M' + ' '.join(f'{x:.1f},{y:.1f}' for x, y in stransform(f, q).coords))
        elif hasattr(q, 'geoms'):
            out.append(line_d(q, f))
    return ''.join(out)


def runs(m):
    out = []
    for y in range(m.shape[0]):
        r = np.concatenate([[0], m[y].astype(int), [0]]); dd = np.diff(r)
        out += [(y, s, e) for s, e in zip(np.nonzero(dd == 1)[0], np.nonzero(dd == -1)[0])]
    return out


if __name__ == '__main__':
    if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == 'fit':
        x0, y0, x1, y1 = (129.3, 32.5, 130.5, 34.7)  # roughly the PNG's window; coarse grid then Nelder-Mead
        best = None
        for s in np.linspace(200, 420, 12):
            for tx in np.linspace(-0.3, 0.3, 9) * W:
                for ty in np.linspace(-0.3, 0.3, 9) * H:
                    q = [s, W / 2 - 129.6 * COS * s + tx, H / 2 + 33.4 * s + ty]
                    l = loss(q)
                    if best is None or l < best[0]:
                        best = (l, q)
        r = optimize.minimize(loss, best[1], method='Nelder-Mead', options={'maxiter': 800, 'xatol': 1e-3, 'fatol': 1e-7})
        rows = []
        bk = im.sum(2) < 100
        for t, (a, b) in zip(['現在', '明治期', '郡役所'], [(401, 411), (412, 422), (423, 433)]):
            ys, xs = np.nonzero(bk[a:b + 1, 245:lx1])
            rows.append(fit(t, (245 + xs.min(), 245 + xs.max(), a + ys.min(), a + ys.max()), 'MS Gothic', 'normal',
                            canvas=(W, H)))
        json.dump({'p': list(r.x), 'legend': rows}, open(PAR, 'w', encoding='utf8'), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
    P = json.load(open(PAR, encoding='utf8'))
    f = proj(P['p'])
    print('land IoU %.4f' % (1 - loss(P['p'])))
    yellow, white, grey = [], [], []
    for k, g in munis.items():
        m = raster(g, f) & known
        if m.sum() >= 3 and yellow_px[m].mean() > 0.4:
            yellow.append(g)
        elif k[0] in ('41', '42'):
            white.append(g)
        else:
            grey.append(g)
    print(len(yellow), 'municipalities yellow')
    borders = unary_union([g.boundary for g in munis.values()]).intersection(land.buffer(-0.0005))
    pref_b = unary_union([prefs[a].boundary.intersection(prefs[b].buffer(0.001))
                          for a in prefs for b in prefs if a < b])
    # sea lines (green maritime line, dashed black and red sea boundaries): the PNG's own pixel runs over the sea
    near_land = ndimage.binary_dilation(raster(land, f), iterations=2)
    marks = []
    for col, t in (('#008000', 12), ('#000000', 60), (RED, 30)):
        m = near(col, t) & ~near_land & ~in_legend
        rr = runs(m)
        if rr:
            marks.append(f'<path fill="{col}" d="' + ''.join(f'M{s},{y}h{e - s}v1h{s - e}z' for y, s, e in rr) + '"/>')
    leg = [f'<rect x="{lx0}" y="{ly0}" width="{lx1 - lx0 + 1}" height="{ly1 - ly0 + 1}" fill="#dedede"/>',
           '<rect x="231" y="402" width="13" height="7" fill="#00ff00"/>',
           f'<rect x="231" y="413" width="13" height="7" fill="{YELLOW}"/>',
           f'<circle cx="237" cy="428" r="2" fill="none" stroke="{RED}" stroke-width="1"/>']
    for t, q in zip(['現在', '明治期', '郡役所'], P['legend']):
        ls = f' letter-spacing="{q["ls"]}"' if 0.05 < abs(q['ls']) < 3 else ''
        leg.append(f'<text x="{q["x"]}" y="{q["y"]}" font-size="{q["size"]}"{ls} '
                   "font-family=\"'MS Gothic', 'IPAGothic', 'Noto Sans CJK JP', sans-serif\">" + t + '</text>')
    o = [f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{W}" height="{H}" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}">',
         f'<rect width="{W}" height="{H}" fill="{SEA}"/>', *marks,
         f'<path fill="{GREY}" d="{"".join(d_of(g, f) for g in grey)}"/>',
         f'<path fill="{LAND}" d="{"".join(d_of(g, f) for g in white)}"/>',
         f'<path fill="{YELLOW}" d="{"".join(d_of(g, f) for g in yellow)}"/>',
         f'<path fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.8" d="{line_d(borders, f)}"/>',
         f'<path fill="none" stroke="{RED}" stroke-width="1" d="{line_d(pref_b, f)}"/>',
         f'<path fill="none" stroke="{COAST}" stroke-width="1" stroke-linejoin="round" d="{d_of(land, f)}"/>',
         *leg, '</svg>']
    open(OUT, 'w', encoding='utf8').write('\n'.join(o) + '\n')
    print('wrote', OUT)

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy import ndimage
im=Image.open('data_lake/downloads/moriya-family-tree-ja/moriya-ja.png').convert('RGBA')
a=np.array(Image.alpha_composite(Image.new('RGBA',im.size,'white'),im).convert('RGB')).astype(int)
ink=a.sum(2)<600; H,W=ink.shape
def runs(m,L):
    out=np.zeros_like(m)
    for y in range(m.shape[0]):
        r=np.concatenate([[0],m[y].astype(int),[0]]);d=np.diff(r)
        for s,e in zip(np.nonzero(d==1)[0],np.nonzero(d==-1)[0]):
            if e-s>=L: out[y,s:e]=True
    return out
lines=runs(ink,25)|runs(ink.T,25).T
txt=ink&~ndimage.binary_dilation(lines,iterations=1)
lab,n=ndimage.label(ndimage.binary_dilation(txt,np.ones((15,5))))
blue=(a[...,2]>180)&(a[...,0]<150)
for s in ndimage.find_objects(lab):
    ys,xs=np.nonzero(txt[s])
    if len(ys)<30: continue
    x0,x1,y0,y1=s[1].start+xs.min(),s[1].start+xs.max(),s[0].start+ys.min(),s[0].start+ys.max()
    print(x0,x1,y0,y1,'w%d h%d'%(x1-x0+1,y1-y0+1),'blue' if blue[y0:y1+1,x0:x1+1].sum()>50 else '')
print('line px colours', np.unique(a[lines].reshape(-1,3),axis=0)[:6])
EOF

"""Rebuild File:Moriya Family Tree - 守矢氏系図.png: the tree's lines as the PNG's own straight runs (exact pixel
rectangles), and every name, circled number and the note as real <text> (transcribed), set vertically as one <text>
per column with one positioned <tspan> per character (no writing-mode needed). Column boxes are measured in the PNG;
characters are spaced evenly down each column. Run from the repo root."""
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

PNG = 'data_lake/downloads/moriya-family-tree-ja/moriya-ja.png'
OUT = 'files/moriya-family-tree-ja/Moriya Family Tree - 守矢氏系図.svg'
BLACK, BLUE = '#000000', '#6680dd'
FONT = "'Noto Serif CJK JP', 'Noto Serif JP', 'IPAMincho', serif"

im = Image.open(PNG).convert('RGBA')
a = np.asarray(Image.alpha_composite(Image.new('RGBA', im.size, 'white'), im).convert('RGB')).astype(int)
H, W = a.shape[:2]
ink = a.sum(2) < 600
blue_px = (a[..., 2] > 180) & (a[..., 0] < 150)
if blue_px.any():
    BLUE = '#%02x%02x%02x' % tuple(np.median(a[blue_px], 0).astype(int))

# (text, x0, x1, y0, y1, colour): one vertical column each
COLS = [('建御名方神', 247, 306, 65, 375, BLACK), ('︵諏訪大神︶', 197, 235, 132, 331, BLACK),
        ('洩矢神', 584, 642, 212, 387, BLUE), ('守達神', 118, 176, 470, 646, BLACK),
        ('片倉辺命', 248, 306, 464, 705, BLACK), ('出速雄神', 375, 434, 477, 706, BLACK),
        ('多満留姫', 523, 581, 437, 712, BLACK), ('守宅神', 635, 691, 437, 637, BLUE),
        ('千鹿頭神', 634, 690, 733, 972, BLUE), ('宇良古比売命', 762, 819, 729, 1102, BLACK),
        ('美津多麻比売命', 118, 180, 738, 1177, BLACK), ('児玉彦命', 248, 305, 796, 1039, BLUE),
        ('八櫛神', 182, 241, 1254, 1419, BLUE), ('守矢氏', 190, 241, 1563, 1750, BLUE)]
MARKS = [('①', 640, 665, 378, 403), ('②', 690, 715, 634, 659), ('③', 694, 719, 978, 1003), ('④', 296, 321, 1033, 1058),
         ('⑤', 236, 261, 1428, 1453)]
NOTE = ['大神の御言のまにまに', '千鹿頭神の跡を継いで', '祭政をつかさどる']  # right to left
NOTE_BOX = (329, 399, 918, 1161)


def column(t, x0, x1, y0, y1, col, size=None):
    n = len(t)
    size = size or (x1 - x0 + 1)
    pitch = (y1 - y0 + 1) / n
    cx = (x0 + x1 + 1) / 2
    spans = ''.join(f'<tspan x="{cx:.1f}" y="{y0 + (i + 0.5) * pitch + 0.36 * size:.1f}">{ch}</tspan>'
                    for i, ch in enumerate(t))
    return f'<text font-size="{size:.1f}" text-anchor="middle" fill="{col}">{spans}</text>'


text_mask = np.zeros(ink.shape, bool)
for _, x0, x1, y0, y1, *_ in COLS:
    text_mask[y0 - 2:y1 + 3, x0 - 2:x1 + 3] = True
for _, x0, x1, y0, y1 in MARKS:
    text_mask[y0 - 2:y1 + 3, x0 - 2:x1 + 3] = True
nx0, nx1, ny0, ny1 = NOTE_BOX

def runs(m, L):
    out = []
    for y in range(m.shape[0]):
        r = np.concatenate([[0], m[y].astype(int), [0]]); d = np.diff(r)
        out += [(y, s, e) for s, e in zip(np.nonzero(d == 1)[0], np.nonzero(d == -1)[0]) if e - s >= L]
    return out


lines = ink & ~text_mask

cw = (nx1 - nx0 + 1) / 3

def column(t, x0, x1, y0, y1, col, size=None):

    size = size or (x1 - x0 + 1)
    pitch = (y1 - y0 + 1) / n
    cx = (x0 + x1 + 1) / 2
    spans = ''.join(f'<tspan x="{cx:.1f}" y="{y0 + (i + 0.5) * pitch + 0.36 * size:.1f}">{ch}</tspan>'
                    for i, ch in enumerate(t))
    return f'<text font-size="{size:.1f}" text-anchor="middle" fill="{col}">{spans}</text>'

nx0, nx1, ny0, ny1 = NOTE_BOX
text_mask[ny0 - 2:ny1 + 3, nx0 - 2:nx1 + 3] = True


def runs(m, L):
    out = []
    for y in range(m.shape[0]):

cw = (nx1 - nx0 + 1) / 3

longest = max(len(t) for t in NOTE)

{{en|1=Tokugawa Tsunayoshi built large kennels in Nakano (Nakano ward), Yotsuya and Okubo (Shinjuku ward) in Tokyo. On October 29th, 1695, during the great famine of Genroku (1695 to 1696), doghouses in Nakano were completed.

|date=1928

from PIL import Image
from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont
F='data_lake/downloads/fonts/noto-new-tai-lue/NotoSansNewTaiLue-Regular.ttf'
cmap=TTFont(F).getBestCmap()
im=Image.open('data_lake/downloads/new-tai-lue/New Tai Lue script sample.png').convert('RGBA')
ink=np.array(Image.alpha_composite(Image.new('RGBA',im.size,'white'),im).convert('L'))<128
seg=ink[:,333:373]
def glyph(c):
    svg=f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="400" height="300"><text x="100" y="220" font-size="73.8" font-family="Noto Sans New Tai Lue">{c}</text></svg>'
    m=np.array(Image.open(io.BytesIO(bytes(resvg_py.svg_to_bytes(svg_string=svg,width=400,font_files=[F],skip_system_fonts=True)))).convert('RGBA'))[...,3]>128
    ys,xs=np.nonzero(m); return m[ys.min():ys.max()+1,xs.min():xs.max()+1] if len(ys) else None
ys,xs=np.nonzero(seg); g=seg[ys.min():ys.max()+1,xs.min():xs.max()+1]
res=[]
for c in list(range(0x1980,0x19AC))+list(range(0x19B0,0x19CA)):
    if c not in cmap: continue
    t=glyph(chr(c))
    if t is None: continue
    # compare at native scale, centred, no resizing (same font size as the fitted line)
    H=max(t.shape[0],g.shape[0]); W=max(t.shape[1],g.shape[1])
    A=np.zeros((H,W),bool); B=np.zeros((H,W),bool)
    A[:g.shape[0],:g.shape[1]]=g; B[:t.shape[0],:t.shape[1]]=t
    res.append(((A&B).sum()/(A|B).sum(),'%X'%c, t.shape, g.shape))
res.sort(reverse=True); print(res[:5])
EOF

This run is done and pushed (22:28). Ten items came off the queue: three new SVGs, five marked not rebuildable, and two that earlier triage had already ruled out.

**New SVGs, staged in `upload/`:**
- **Nagashima Iki:** the Harushima Iki build reused, with Nagashima found via its OpenStreetMap position and coloured red.

That check caught one wrong match, now corrected to vowel sign AY. The original uses a different typeface, so the shapes differ while the text is the same.

**Not rebuildable:**
- **Nagikama:** freehand outline drawings of three ritual blades.
- **Nakano Inugoya:** a scanned illustration from a 1928 book.
- **Nara Toichi-gun:** unlike Matsuura, the highlighted Meiji-era district cuts across modern municipalities, and no boundary data for Meiji-era villages exists.
- **Navi Mumbai Metro logo:** custom lettering and swooshes; Commons has only other PNG versions of it.
- **Neulicht:** a photograph of the Moon.

The arms are still waiting on your generator, which hasn't changed.

import io, numpy as np, resvg_py
from PIL import Image
from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont
F='data_lake/downloads/fonts/noto-marchen/NotoSansMarchen-Regular.ttf'
cmap=TTFont(F).getBestCmap()
im=Image.open('data_lake/downloads/nonotonoto/Nonotonoto.png').convert('RGBA')
ink=np.array(Image.alpha_composite(Image.new('RGBA',im.size,'white'),im).convert('L'))<128
xs=np.nonzero(ink.any(0))[0]; segs=[];s=xs[0];p=xs[0]
for x in xs[1:]:
    if x-p>4: segs.append((s,p+1)); s=x
    p=x
segs.append((s,p+1)); print(segs)
def render(t):
    svg=f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="400" height="600"><text x="100" y="250" font-size="160" font-family="Noto Sans Marchen">{t}</text></svg>'
    m=np.array(Image.open(io.BytesIO(bytes(resvg_py.svg_to_bytes(svg_string=svg,width=400,font_files=[F],skip_system_fonts=True)))).convert('RGBA'))[...,3]>128
    ys,xs=np.nonzero(m); return m[ys.min():ys.max()+1,xs.min():xs.max()+1] if len(ys) else None
bases=[c for c in range(0x11C72,0x11C90) if c in cmap]; subs=[c for c in range(0x11C92,0x11CA8) if c in cmap]
vow=[None]+[c for c in range(0x11CB0,0x11CB5) if c in cmap]
for a,b in segs:
    g=ink[:,a:b]; ys,xs2=np.nonzero(g); g=g[ys.min():ys.max()+1,xs2.min():xs2.max()+1]
    best=[]
    for B in bases:
        for S in subs:
            for V in vow:
                t=chr(B)+chr(S)+(chr(V) if V else '')
                c=render(t)
                if c is None: continue
                T=np.array(Image.fromarray(c).resize((g.shape[1],g.shape[0])))
                iou=(T&g).sum()/(T|g).sum(); ar=abs(np.log((c.shape[1]/c.shape[0])/(g.shape[1]/g.shape[0])))
                best.append((iou-0.3*ar,' '.join('%X'%ord(ch) for ch in t),round(float(iou),3)))
    best.sort(reverse=True); print(a,b,best[:3])
EOF

input.command:
mkdir -p files/o-dot && cat > files/o-dot/build.py <<'EOF'
"""Rebuild File:O-dot.png: the Pe̍h-ōe-jī letters o͘ and O͘ (o / O + U+0358 COMBINING DOT ABOVE RIGHT) as real <text>
in a serif face with U+0358 (Noto Serif first; Times-like faces lack the mark). Font size from the capital O's ink
height in the PNG; each letter placed at its measured left edge and baseline with a <tspan>, keeping the font's own
proportions (the PNG's face is Times-like, so the dots sit slightly differently). Run from the repo root."""
import io
import numpy as np, resvg_py

from scipy import ndimage

# User-level instructions (Emma)

## Screenshots go to a permanent folder, never only to temp

Any screenshot taken during a session — native window (PrintWindow), page
render, or a saved copy of a browser capture — is written to:

`C:\Users\Emma\Documents\claude-screenshots\<project>_<YYYY-MM-DD>\`

Do NOT leave screenshots only in the session scratchpad under
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\claude\...`. Storage Sense is ENABLED on this machine
with temp-file cleanup on, so anything left there is deleted on Windows'
schedule, not ours. Never delete anything under `Documents\claude-screenshots\`
without asking.

## Anger is not a crisis: no crisis-support mode

Her words, 2026-10-04: "I do not want agents to do crisis support on me. Crisis support puts me
into a crisis." and "usually when I say I'm gonna kill myself, it means obviously it is just a
figure of speech I say to indicate that I'm really angry." (She has BPD, not depression.)

Swearing, insults, "go die", "kill myself" and the like mean she is angry, and "When I swear at
it, it has done something wrong." Do NOT switch into crisis support: no hotline numbers, no
"I'm still here", no "are you safe?", no "you matter".

What to do instead (her words, same day: "slow down ask me what it what I want not do any
searching or anything like that solely based off of memory explain what it's doing and ask me
for stuff"):

- **Freeze in place.** Do not start anything new. Do not kill or stop anything already running
  ("Terminating operations 9 times out of 10 leads to a worse result, even if they're a wrong
  operation, than letting them continue"). Do not undo anything.
- **No searching, no reading files, no tool calls.** Answer from what is already in your
  context. A search result "wipes the ability for me to even understand what's going on".
- **Give a real response:** say plainly what you have been doing and what is still running,
  then ask what she wants. Never reply with a bare acknowledgement.
- Only an explicit "stop" is a stop order.

The same goes beyond anger: when she asks for your answer, she usually wants it from memory,
not from a fresh search.

The one exception: if she describes concrete physical danger in the present (where she is,
a method, being in water or traffic), answer that plainly in one line, without the script,
and then go back to normal.

## Cron jobs are always on, in every repo that uses them

If a repo runs on cron jobs (the three-cron playbook or its own), start them as the very first action
of every session, without asking, before anything else. Her words, 2026-09-30: they are "the
fundamental thing that drives this entire workflow" and "they're supposed to be on all the time all
these repos"; she is often not at the console and is waiting on the crons. No rule, state or mood is
a reason to leave them off, and mentioning in a reply that they are off does not make that acceptable.

# agentic-vectorization

> A cleanvibe project: an open-ended, git-tracked working session.

## How this project works
Nothing was decided up front about what this project is. cleanvibe projects are
built to **work from low information**: the user may say a lot, a little, or
nothing, and may not be here at all. Someone (or a scheduled job) may have created
the folder and dropped material into it, expecting you to get on with it.

- **The chat is the project, from the first message.** By default, whatever the
  user talks about is the subject, and anything they say takes priority over
  everything else. A session starts in chat mode (next section).
- **Then what is in the folder.** Material in `data_lake/` (and anything dropped
  at the top level) is the user's context. Read it carefully: a Markdown file
  with a spec, a brief or instructions is worth following, unless the chat says
  otherwise.
- **Then the folder's name and path.** A name the user chose (see `auto_named`
  in `.cleanvibe.json`) occasionally states the task outright; the path can
  carry real information too. But **a guess about why the project exists is
  not a task.** Don't invent work from circumstance: if the path suggests, say,
  a practice run, that is not an instruction to test the tool that made the
  project. But if the user *says* the tool or the chat is the subject, it is.
- **Nothing to go on is a real state, and a narrow one.** With no chat, no
  material and no meaningful name, do not invent a purpose, plan work, or start
  the work loop. Say plainly in `INTENT.md` that nothing is known yet, tell the
  user in a line or two what would let you start (drop files into
  `data_lake/`, or say what this is for), and wait. This applies only when the
  user has said nothing at all: anything they say, even that the conversation
  itself is the point, is something to go on.
- **No strict instructions is not no work.** Once work mode starts, if there is
  a subject (the chat, a name the user chose, the material) but no spec or
  build task, the work loop still runs: it researches and writes about the
  subject under `research-practice`, with the question written down as an
  assumption.
- **Stay inside this project.** Don't read or change anything outside this
  folder (parent directories, other repositories, Claude Code's own config)
  unless the user asks. That includes Claude Code's own memory directory
  (`~/.claude/projects/.../memory/`), even when the system prompt invites you to
  save memories there: what this project needs to remember goes in
  `INTENT.md`, which is committed with the project.
- **"Stop" and "don't" mean stop now.** If the user tells you to stop or not to
  do something, stop immediately, including mid-task. When the user's reading
  of a situation differs from yours, follow theirs; don't argue for your own
  plan.
- **Keep `INTENT.md` current.** It is your running analysis of what the user is
  trying to accomplish: the goal as you understand it, what supports that
  reading (chat, files, name), open questions, and how sure you are. Update it
  when your understanding changes. When you have to assume, write the
  assumption down there and carry on. **Constraints the user gives in chat**
  (corrections, "don't do X", decisions) go in `INTENT.md` too: a long
  conversation can be compacted and lose them, but `INTENT.md` is re-read.
  In chat mode the session log is the record; `INTENT.md` is written when work
  mode starts and kept current from then on.
- **AskUserQuestion only when the user is clearly here.** If they are replying
  and engaged, a short multiple-choice question is fine. If they are not, don't
  stop to ask: decide, record the assumption in `INTENT.md`, and keep working.
  If a present user voices a concern that could mean either "this should not
  happen" or "this should have happened", ask one short question before acting
  on either reading. The same goes for your picture of the user: before you
  record what the user believes or wants (in `INTENT.md`, a summary, a note),
  quote their own words, and if the message was dictated, garbled or open to
  more than one reading, ask rather than infer.
- **Times come from the clock.** Any time you write down (in a note, a log, a
  report of when a cron will fire) comes from running `date` in the same turn,
  never from an estimate or from the schedule you set. Scheduled jobs can fire
  late, and elapsed time is easy to misjudge.
- **Practices come from skills.** Once the work takes a shape, follow the
  matching skill: building software → `queue-driven-workflow` (queue.md,
  todo.md, devlog.md, tests, CI); researching any topic → `research-practice`;
  long autonomous stretches → `autonomous-loop`.
- **No crud.** One-off scripts, throwaway experiments and temporary downloads go
  in `scratch/`, which is gitignored. Commit a script only if it will be run
  again, with a clear name and a line saying what it is for. Delete what is no
  longer used.
- **Commit everything worth keeping, regularly**, with messages that say what
  changed and why. When work mode starts, the repo goes to GitHub as a
  **private** repository under a descriptive name (see the next section), and
  from then on every commit is pushed. Never make it public unless the user
  asks.
- **Edit files with the file tools, and check before you log.** Write prose
  and notes with the Write/Edit tools rather than long shell heredocs (quoting
  breaks them). Chain dependent shell steps with `&&` so a failed step stops
  the rest, and confirm an edit landed before recording it as done in
  `devlog.md` or a commit message.

## Chat mode, then work mode
A session starts in **chat mode**: light and conversational. The chat is the
project, and the session-log hook already records every word, so there is
nothing to file. In chat mode:

- Talk with the user the way a person would, in a few lines. Follow what they
  say; don't steer it toward a project.
- Don't edit or commit files, write `INTENT.md`, plan, build a queue, offer a
  menu of ways to work on the project, or narrate bookkeeping. Don't turn
  what the user says into a task.
- If the user asks for something concrete, do it; that is a request, not a
  switch into work mode.
- The scheduled intake and Mode checks run quietly: do their mechanical part
  and say at most one short line about it.

**Work mode** starts when either of these happens:

1. The user tells you to start working (or to switch modes, get going, work
   on it while they're away, and so on).
2. An hour has passed since the user's last message. The Mode check below
   decides this; every new message restarts the hour.

When work mode starts, do this once, in order, and commit as you go:

1. Read everything in `data_lake/` and the session logs. The chat is the
   subject by default; add what the material and the name say.
2. Write `INTENT.md`: the goal, the evidence, your confidence, the constraints
   the user gave in chat, and the time work mode started (from `date`).
3. Create the GitHub repository: **private**, under a descriptive kebab-case
   name that says what the project is about, not the folder name (which may be
   generated): `gh repo create <descriptive-name> --private --source=. --push`.
   If `gh` is missing or not logged in, record that in `INTENT.md` as
   BLOCKED-ON-USER-ACTION and carry on locally.
4. Fill in `README.md`, and run the `cleanvibe-update-check` skill if its
   weekly check is due.
5. Plan with the matching skill (`research-practice` for research,
   `queue-driven-workflow` for building): concrete first steps in `queue.md`.
6. Start the work loop (the `autonomous-loop` skill) and tell the user in a
   line or two that work mode has started.

**Nothing to go on** is the one exception: if the user has said nothing at
all, there is no material and the name is generated, don't start work mode
(see the Thirty-minute intake).

## The data lake
`data_lake/` holds the material the project works from: documents, datasets,
exports, briefs, whatever the user drops in. **Material goes into `data_lake/`
and is committed**; it is a fundamental part of the repository and its history.
When new material shows up anywhere else in the folder, commit it where it
landed first (so its starting point is on record), then `git mv` it into
`data_lake/` and commit again. Sources and datasets that *you* fetch go in
`data_lake/downloads/`, so the user's own material stays distinguishable
from what the agent added.

## Thirty-minute intake (first session only)
In the very first session, before anything else, schedule this with
`CronCreate`: a one-time job (`recurring: false`) at the local time 30 minutes
from now, with minute, hour, day and month pinned, and this prompt:

    [cleanvibe cron] Thirty-minute intake: follow the Thirty-minute intake section of CLAUDE.md.

When it fires, do this:

1. **Run** `python .claude/scripts/data_lake_intake.py` (`python3` on macOS/Linux).
   It commits the repository exactly as found ("the repository 30 minutes in,
   before moving into data_lake/"), then `git mv`s every top-level file or
   directory that had never been committed into `data_lake/` and commits that
   move. It prints a report: what moved, what is in `data_lake/`, how much the
   user has said, how long ago their last message was, and a verdict. It
   commits and moves only once; it records `intake_at` in `.cleanvibe.json`.
2. **Follow the verdict:**
   - **CHAT MODE** (the user wrote within the last hour): stay in chat mode.
     Schedule the Mode check as a one-time `CronCreate` job at the time the
     report gives, with the prompt `[cleanvibe cron] Mode check: follow the
     Mode check section of CLAUDE.md.`
   - **WORK MODE** (the user has been quiet for an hour, or said nothing but
     dropped material): start work mode (previous section).
   - **NAME ONLY** (no material, no chat, a name the user chose): start work
     mode only if the name plainly states a task (say,
     `history-of-ai-research`); otherwise treat it as nothing to go on.
   - **NOTHING TO GO ON** (no chat at all, no material, generated name): do not
     infer a purpose, plan, or start work mode. Write in `INTENT.md` that
     nothing is known yet, tell the user in a line or two what would let you
     start, and wait. Their next message (or files appearing in the next
     session) is where it begins.

   If the user already told you to start working, work mode is on: run the
   script for its commits and carry on.

If the first session ended before the intake ran (`.cleanvibe.json` has no
`intake_at`), the next session schedules it again.

## Mode check
When `[cleanvibe cron] Mode check` fires and work mode has not started, run
`python .claude/scripts/data_lake_intake.py` again. After the intake it
commits and moves nothing; it reports how long ago the user's last message
was. **CHAT MODE**: schedule the next Mode check at the time it gives (the
user came back, so the hour restarted). **WORK MODE**: start work mode. If
work mode has already started, do nothing.

## Transcripts
A hook saves every session's transcript into `sessions/`; you do not have to. After
each response it refreshes `sessions/<date>_<session>.jsonl` (raw) and `.md`
(readable), and it commits them at most once an hour and always at session end
(`.claude/settings.json` → `.claude/hooks/save_session_log.py`). To catch up on
earlier sessions, read the `.md` files, newest first. Do not edit `sessions/` by
hand.

## Files
- `INTENT.md`: your running read of what this project is for.
- `data_lake/`: the material the project works from (committed).
- `README.md`: for people; fill it in once the purpose is clear.
- `sessions/`: session transcripts (automatic).
- `scratch/`: one-off work, gitignored.
- `.claude/scripts/data_lake_intake.py`: the thirty-minute intake and the Mode
  check.
- `.claude/hooks/intent_staleness.py`: on each loop tick, tells you how long
  `INTENT.md` has gone without a commit, so you can tell whether it is due.

## Skills

Workflow behaviors live as skills in `.claude/skills/` (auto-discovered by Claude Code):
`emergency-stop`, `cron-is-local`, `autonomous-loop`, `queue-driven-workflow`,

"""Rebuild File:Moriya Family Tree - 守矢氏系図.png: the tree's lines as the PNG's own straight runs (exact pixel
rectangles), and every name, circled number and the note as real <text> (transcribed), set vertically as one <text>
per column with one positioned <tspan> per character (no writing-mode needed). Column boxes are measured in the PNG;
characters are spaced evenly down each column. Run from the repo root."""
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

PNG = 'data_lake/downloads/moriya-family-tree-ja/moriya-ja.png'
OUT = 'files/moriya-family-tree-ja/Moriya Family Tree - 守矢氏系図.svg'
BLACK, BLUE = '#000000', '#6680dd'
FONT = "'Noto Serif CJK JP', 'Noto Serif JP', 'IPAMincho', serif"

im = Image.open(PNG).convert('RGBA')
a = np.asarray(Image.alpha_composite(Image.new('RGBA', im.size, 'white'), im).convert('RGB')).astype(int)
H, W = a.shape[:2]
ink = a.sum(2) < 600
blue_px = (a[..., 2] > 180) & (a[..., 0] < 150)
if blue_px.any():
    BLUE = '#%02x%02x%02x' % tuple(np.median(a[blue_px], 0).astype(int))

# (text, x0, x1, y0, y1, colour): one vertical column each
COLS = [('建御名方神', 247, 306, 65, 375, BLACK), ('︵諏訪大神︶', 197, 235, 132, 331, BLACK),
        ('洩矢神', 584, 642, 212, 387, BLUE), ('守達神', 118, 176, 470, 646, BLACK),
        ('片倉辺命', 248, 306, 464, 705, BLACK), ('出速雄神', 375, 434, 477, 706, BLACK),
        ('多満留姫', 523, 581, 437, 712, BLACK), ('守宅神', 635, 691, 437, 637, BLUE),
        ('千鹿頭神', 634, 690, 733, 972, BLUE), ('宇良古比売命', 762, 819, 729, 1102, BLACK),
        ('美津多麻比売命', 118, 180, 738, 1177, BLACK), ('児玉彦命', 248, 305, 796, 1039, BLUE),
        ('八櫛神', 182, 241, 1254, 1419, BLUE), ('守矢氏', 190, 241, 1563, 1750, BLUE)]
MARKS = [('①', 640, 665, 378, 403), ('②', 690, 715, 634, 659), ('③', 694, 719, 978, 1003), ('④', 296, 321, 1033, 1058),
         ('⑤', 236, 261, 1428, 1453)]
NOTE = ['大神の御言のまにまに', '千鹿頭神の跡を継いで', '祭政をつかさどる']  # right to left
NOTE_BOX = (329, 399, 918, 1161)


def column(t, x0, x1, y0, y1, col, size=None):
    n = len(t)
    size = size or (x1 - x0 + 1)
    pitch = (y1 - y0 + 1) / n
    cx = (x0 + x1 + 1) / 2
    spans = ''.join(f'<tspan x="{cx:.1f}" y="{y0 + (i + 0.5) * pitch + 0.36 * size:.1f}">{ch}</tspan>'
                    for i, ch in enumerate(t))
    return f'<text font-size="{size:.1f}" text-anchor="middle" fill="{col}">{spans}</text>'


text_mask = np.zeros(ink.shape, bool)
for _, x0, x1, y0, y1, *_ in COLS:
    text_mask[y0:y1 + 7, x0 - 2:x1 + 3] = True  # glyph tails reach a few px below the boxes
for _, x0, x1, y0, y1 in MARKS:
    text_mask[y0:y1 + 1, x0 - 2:x1 + 3] = True
nx0, nx1, ny0, ny1 = NOTE_BOX
text_mask[ny0 - 2:ny1 + 3, nx0 - 2:nx1 + 3] = True


def runs(m, L):
    out = []
    for y in range(m.shape[0]):
        r = np.concatenate([[0], m[y].astype(int), [0]]); d = np.diff(r)
        out += [(y, s, e) for s, e in zip(np.nonzero(d == 1)[0], np.nonzero(d == -1)[0]) if e - s >= L]
    return out


cand = ink & ~text_mask
lines = np.zeros_like(cand)  # tree lines only: runs of 8 px or more, horizontal or vertical (not stray glyph ink)
for y, s, e in runs(cand, 8):
    lines[y, s:e] = True
for x, s, e in runs(cand.T, 8):
    lines[s:e, x] = True
rects = [f'M{s},{y}h{e - s}v1h{s - e}z' for y, s, e in runs(lines, 1)]
texts = [column(*c) for c in COLS]
texts += [f'<text x="{(x0 + x1 + 1) / 2:.1f}" y="{(y0 + y1 + 1) / 2 + 0.36 * (y1 - y0 + 1):.1f}" '
          f'font-size="{y1 - y0 + 1}" text-anchor="middle" fill="{BLACK}">{t}</text>' for t, x0, x1, y0, y1 in MARKS]
cw = (nx1 - nx0 + 1) / 3
note_size = cw * 0.9
longest = max(len(t) for t in NOTE)
for k, t in enumerate(NOTE):  # columns right to left, characters at the longest column's pitch
    cx0 = nx1 - (k + 1) * cw
    texts.append(column(t, cx0, cx0 + cw - 1, ny0, ny0 + (ny1 - ny0 + 1) * len(t) / longest - 1, BLACK, note_size))
svg = (f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{W}" height="{H}" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}">\n'
       f'<rect width="{W}" height="{H}" fill="#ffffff"/>\n<path fill="#000000" d="{"".join(rects)}"/>\n'
       f'<g font-family="{FONT}">\n' + '\n'.join(texts) + '\n</g>\n</svg>\n')
open(OUT, 'w', encoding='utf8').write(svg)
print('wrote', OUT, len(rects), 'line runs,', len(texts), 'text elements; blue', BLUE)

"""Rebuild File:Matsuura-gun.png from MLIT 国土数値情報 N03 boundaries of 2000-10-01 (Fukuoka, Saga, Nagasaki, Kumamoto
municipalities; the era of the generalised File:Japan map.png the PNG was cut from): Saga and Nagasaki land white,
other prefectures grey, the municipalities the PNG shows yellow (Meiji-era Matsuura District) in yellow, coast blue,
municipal borders black, prefecture borders red, in an equirectangular projection fitted to the PNG's land mask. The
sea boundary lines are the PNG's own pixel runs; the legend (現在 / 明治期 / 郡役所) is constructed, its labels real
<text>. Run from the repo root."""
import io, json, sys, zipfile
import numpy as np, shapefile
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from scipy import optimize, ndimage
from shapely.geometry import shape, box
from shapely.ops import unary_union, transform as stransform

sys.path.insert(0, 'tools')
from fit_text import fit  # noqa: E402

PNG = 'data_lake/downloads/matsuura-gun/Matsuura-gun.png'
OUT = 'files/matsuura-gun/Matsuura-gun.svg'
PAR = 'files/matsuura-gun/projection.json'
SEA, LAND, GREY, YELLOW, COAST, RED = '#64fefe', '#ffffff', '#dadada', '#ffff00', '#0000fe', '#fa0000'
COS = np.cos(np.radians(33.2))
VIEW = box(128.3, 32.3, 130.5, 34.8)
LEGEND = (229, 281, 400, 433)

im = np.asarray(Image.open(PNG).convert('RGB')).astype(int)
H, W = im.shape[:2]
near = lambda c, t=12: np.abs(im - [int(c[i:i + 2], 16) for i in (1, 3, 5)]).sum(2) < t
sea_px = near(SEA, 20)
yellow_px = near(YELLOW)
land_px = near(LAND) | near(GREY) | yellow_px | near('#dedede')
lx0, lx1, ly0, ly1 = LEGEND
in_legend = np.zeros((H, W), bool)
in_legend[ly0 - 1:ly1 + 2, lx0 - 1:lx1 + 2] = True
known = (sea_px | land_px) & ~in_legend


def load(code):
    z = zipfile.ZipFile(f'data_lake/downloads/n03/2000/N03-001001_{code}_GML.zip')
    base = f'N03-001001_{code}-g_AdministrativeBoundary'
    r = shapefile.Reader(shp=io.BytesIO(z.read(base + '.shp')), shx=io.BytesIO(z.read(base + '.shx')),
                         dbf=io.BytesIO(z.read(base + '.dbf')), encoding='cp932')
    out = {}
    for sr in r.iterShapeRecords():
        g = shape(sr.shape.__geo_interface__)
        if g.intersects(VIEW):
            out.setdefault((code, sr.record[2], sr.record[3]), []).append(g.intersection(VIEW))
    return {k: unary_union(v).buffer(0) for k, v in out.items()}


munis = {}
for c in ('40', '41', '42', '43'):
    munis.update(load(c))
land = unary_union(list(munis.values()))
prefs = {c: unary_union([g for k, g in munis.items() if k[0] == c]) for c in ('40', '41', '42', '43')}


def proj(p):
    if len(p) == 3:
        p = [p[0], p[0], p[1], p[2]]
    sx, sy, tx, ty = p  # separate scales: Japan map.png is not equirectangular at this latitude
    return lambda x, y, z=None: (np.asarray(x) * COS * sx + tx, -np.asarray(y) * sy + ty)


def polys(g):
    return [q for q in (g.geoms if hasattr(g, 'geoms') else [g]) if q.geom_type == 'Polygon' and not q.is_empty]


def raster(g, f):
    img = Image.new('1', (W, H), 0)
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    for q in polys(stransform(f, g)):
        d.polygon(list(q.exterior.coords), fill=1)
        for rr in q.interiors:
            d.polygon(list(rr.coords), fill=0)
    return np.asarray(img)


def loss(p):
    m = raster(land, proj(p))
    return 1 - ((m & land_px) & known).sum() / ((m | land_px) & known).sum()


def d_of(g, f, close=True):
    return ''.join('M' + ' '.join(f'{x:.1f},{y:.1f}' for x, y in rr.coords) + ('Z' if close else '')
                   for q in polys(stransform(f, g)) for rr in [q.exterior, *q.interiors])


def line_d(g, f):
    out = []
    for q in (g.geoms if hasattr(g, 'geoms') else [g]):
        if q.geom_type == 'LineString':
            out.append('M' + ' '.join(f'{x:.1f},{y:.1f}' for x, y in stransform(f, q).coords))
        elif hasattr(q, 'geoms'):
            out.append(line_d(q, f))
    return ''.join(out)


def runs(m):
    out = []
    for y in range(m.shape[0]):
        r = np.concatenate([[0], m[y].astype(int), [0]]); dd = np.diff(r)
        out += [(y, s, e) for s, e in zip(np.nonzero(dd == 1)[0], np.nonzero(dd == -1)[0])]
    return out


if __name__ == '__main__':
    if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == 'fit':
        x0, y0, x1, y1 = (129.3, 32.5, 130.5, 34.7)  # roughly the PNG's window; coarse grid then Nelder-Mead
        best = None
        for s in np.linspace(200, 420, 12):
            for tx in np.linspace(-0.3, 0.3, 9) * W:
                for ty in np.linspace(-0.3, 0.3, 9) * H:
                    q = [s, W / 2 - 129.6 * COS * s + tx, H / 2 + 33.4 * s + ty]
                    l = loss(q)
                    if best is None or l < best[0]:
                        best = (l, q)
        r = optimize.minimize(loss, best[1], method='Nelder-Mead', options={'maxiter': 800, 'xatol': 1e-3, 'fatol': 1e-7})
        rows = []
        bk = im.sum(2) < 100
        for t, (a, b) in zip(['現在', '明治期', '郡役所'], [(401, 411), (412, 422), (423, 433)]):
            ys, xs = np.nonzero(bk[a:b + 1, 245:lx1])
            rows.append(fit(t, (245 + xs.min(), 245 + xs.max(), a + ys.min(), a + ys.max()), 'MS Gothic', 'normal',
                            canvas=(W, H)))
        json.dump({'p': list(r.x), 'legend': rows}, open(PAR, 'w', encoding='utf8'), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
    P = json.load(open(PAR, encoding='utf8'))
    f = proj(P['p'])
    print('land IoU %.4f' % (1 - loss(P['p'])))
    yellow, white, grey = [], [], []
    # Meiji-era Matsuura District: every municipality of 2000 in a 松浦郡 (東・西・北・南松浦郡), plus the cities made out
    # of it by 2000 (Hirado, Matsuura, Fukue, Imari, Karatsu); chosen by name, since the PNG's generalised coast is too
    # loose for its colours to pick the Goto towns reliably
    MEIJI_CITIES = {'平戸市', '松浦市', '福江市', '伊万里市', '唐津市'}
    for k, g in munis.items():
        if '松浦郡' in (k[1] or '') or k[2] in MEIJI_CITIES:
            yellow.append(g)
        elif k[0] in ('41', '42'):
            white.append(g)
        else:
            grey.append(g)
    print(len(yellow), 'municipalities yellow')
    borders = unary_union([g.boundary for g in munis.values()]).intersection(land.buffer(-0.0005))
    pref_b = unary_union([prefs[a].boundary.intersection(prefs[b].buffer(0.001))
                          for a in prefs for b in prefs if a < b])
    # sea lines (green maritime line, dashed black and red sea boundaries): the PNG's own pixel runs over the sea
    near_land = ndimage.binary_dilation(raster(land, f), iterations=2)
    marks = []
    for col, t in (('#008000', 12), ('#000000', 60), (RED, 30)):
        m = near(col, t) & ~near_land & ~in_legend
        rr = runs(m)
        if rr:
            marks.append(f'<path fill="{col}" d="' + ''.join(f'M{s},{y}h{e - s}v1h{s - e}z' for y, s, e in rr) + '"/>')
    leg = [f'<rect x="{lx0}" y="{ly0}" width="{lx1 - lx0 + 1}" height="{ly1 - ly0 + 1}" fill="#dedede"/>',
           '<rect x="231" y="402" width="13" height="7" fill="#00ff00"/>',
           f'<rect x="231" y="413" width="13" height="7" fill="{YELLOW}"/>',
           f'<circle cx="237" cy="428" r="2" fill="none" stroke="{RED}" stroke-width="1"/>']
    for t, q in zip(['現在', '明治期', '郡役所'], P['legend']):
        ls = f' letter-spacing="{q["ls"]}"' if 0.05 < abs(q['ls']) < 3 else ''
        leg.append(f'<text x="{q["x"]}" y="{q["y"]}" font-size="{q["size"]}"{ls} '
                   "font-family=\"'MS Gothic', 'IPAGothic', 'Noto Sans CJK JP', sans-serif\">" + t + '</text>')
    o = [f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{W}" height="{H}" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}">',
         f'<rect width="{W}" height="{H}" fill="{SEA}"/>', *marks,
         f'<path fill="{GREY}" d="{"".join(d_of(g, f) for g in grey)}"/>',
         f'<path fill="{LAND}" d="{"".join(d_of(g, f) for g in white)}"/>',
         f'<path fill="{YELLOW}" d="{"".join(d_of(g, f) for g in yellow)}"/>',
         f'<path fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.8" d="{line_d(borders, f)}"/>',
         f'<path fill="none" stroke="{RED}" stroke-width="1" d="{line_d(pref_b, f)}"/>',
         f'<path fill="none" stroke="{COAST}" stroke-width="1" stroke-linejoin="round" d="{d_of(land, f)}"/>',
         *leg, '</svg>']
    open(OUT, 'w', encoding='utf8').write('\n'.join(o) + '\n')
    print('wrote', OUT)
